brief.title: Close Northfield
brief.audience: The board of a mid-sized manufacturer
brief.objective: Approve closing the Northfield line and redeploying its volume, or reject it with a stated alternative
brief.visualDirection: Authored for this deck; see creativeDirection.

narrative: By the end the board should approve the closure, because the line loses money at every volume it can actually reach.

alternatives.name: Single number
alternatives.thesis: One figure per slide, at a size that leaves nowhere to hide, with the qualification set small beside it
alternatives.differentiator: Extreme sparsity: at most one number and one sentence per slide until the recommendation

alternatives.name: Bridge
alternatives.thesis: A waterfall carrying the reader from today's margin to the proposed one
alternatives.differentiator: A single chart repeated with changing emphasis
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A bridge invites arguing with the steps; the board needs to argue with the decision

sequencePlan.narrativeJob: Show the loss at a size nobody can look past

sequencePlan.narrativeJob: Show that the volume required is not reachable

creativeDirection.name: Single number
creativeDirection.concept: A board paper that refuses to hide behind density: one figure per page, at a size that leaves nowhere to look away to
creativeDirection.rationale: This board reads the appendix. The deck's job is to make the decision unavoidable, not to restate the model
creativeDirection.geometryLanguage: Nothing but type and one hairline. No shapes, no fills, no containers
creativeDirection.spatialRhythm: Very wide margins throughout; the page is mostly empty and stays that way
creativeDirection.materialLanguage: Ink on cartridge paper; a single red reserved for the loss

single-figure.description: One number, very large, with its qualification set small beside it
single-figure.meaning: Nothing here is being hidden in an average

hard: No slide carries more than one figure above 40pt
Every figure names its source line
soft: Leave the lower third of most slides empty

avoid: charts with more than two series

title: Recommendation
designIntent: The recommendation first. A board that has to wait four slides for it reads ahead anyway.
composition: One line of type in the upper left; a hairline under it; the rest of the page empty.

text: BOARD PAPER 26/04 — FOR DECISION
Close the Northfield line at the end of Q3 and redeploy its volume to Southgate and Ellis.
The line has not covered its attributable fixed cost in nine quarters and cannot at any volume it can reach.

notes: Read the recommendation verbatim, then stop talking.

sources.label: Management accounts, FY25 and FY26 to date

title: FY25 contribution
designIntent: One figure, enormous. Everything else on the page is a footnote to it.
composition: The figure occupies the left two-thirds; its qualification is a small column at the right.

text: FY25 CONTRIBUTION, NORTHFIELD
After directly attributable fixed cost. Before any allocation of group overhead, which would make it worse.
Nine consecutive quarters below zero. FY24 was −£1.7m on the same basis.
Management accounts, FY25 and FY26 to date.

notes: Do not soften the number. It is the paper.

sources.label: Management accounts, FY25 and FY26 to date

title: The volume it would take
designIntent: The number that closes the argument: break-even is above the plant's ceiling, so no plan reaches it.
composition: Two lines of type on the left third; a two-bar chart occupying the right.

text: Break-even is above the ceiling.
Northfield breaks even at 118,000 units. Sustained capacity at the current shift pattern is 96,000. The gap is not a demand problem.

alt: Sustained capacity is 96,000 units a year against a break-even volume of 118,000

text: Plant capacity study, engineering, January 2026; management accounts.

notes: If anyone proposes a third shift, the capacity study covers it in appendix C.

title: Where the volume goes
designIntent: Quiet and factual. Two rows is the whole answer; a longer table would imply more uncertainty than there is.
composition: A short table set in the vertical middle with very wide margins.

text: Where the volume goes
The remaining 21,000 units are low-margin contract work we would not renew. That is the intent, not a shortfall.
Plant capacity study, engineering, January 2026.

notes: Be explicit that we are choosing to drop the last 21,000 units.

title: What would make this wrong
designIntent: Three lines, low on the page. Naming the risks is what earns the recommendation.
composition: Three rows in the lower half; the upper half deliberately empty.

text: What would make this wrong
Closure cost
£3.1m central estimate, and it is management's, not audited.
Payback moves from 14 months to 22 if it lands 40% high.
Southgate ramp
Absorbing 54,000 units assumes no change to the shift pattern.
A ramp slip pushes the saving into FY27.
Customer loss
Two contracts are Northfield-specific by name, not by capability.
We estimate one of the two is genuinely at risk.
The closure-cost estimate is not yet independently reviewed and is marked as such in the claim ledger.

notes: Volunteer the unreviewed estimate before anyone asks about it.

title: The resolution
designIntent: The words the board is being asked to pass, not a summary of them.
composition: A block of resolution text in the upper left; a signature rule and date beneath.

text: RESOLUTION PUT TO THE BOARD

That the Northfield line be closed with effect from 30 September 2026; that its volume be redeployed to Southgate and Ellis without capital expenditure; and that the closure provision of £3.1 m be recognised in Q3, subject to independent review of that estimate before the July meeting.
Chair
Date
If the board rejects this, the alternative on the table is a third shift, which the capacity study prices at £4.8 m of capital.

notes: Read the resolution word for word. The rejection alternative is on the slide so nobody has to ask.
